s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive cerebellopontine angle syndrome with headache and neurologic deficits
salient_findings: Large lobulated mass at the left cerebellopontine angle
key_facts: 3-month history of worsening symptoms
Headache exacerbated by Valsalva maneuvers
Bilateral past-pointing on neurologic examination
Intention tremor on neurologic examination
6.9 × 5.5 × 6.1 cm mass centered at the left cerebellopontine angle
Mass extends craniocaudally from the left ambient cistern to the premedullary space
Involvement and expansion of Meckel’s cave
Small extension into the left infratemporal fossa via the foramen ovale
Cystic areas with interspersed enhancing septa on MRI
Solid components with T1/T2-isointense enhancement on MRI
Hemorrhagic foci on susceptibility-weighted imaging
Compression of the left cerebellum and brainstem
Dilation of the third, fourth, and lateral ventricles

shortlist.label: Vestibular schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Common cause of cerebellopontine angle syndrome with gradual onset of symptoms

shortlist.label: Meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of progressive cerebellopontine angle syndrome with cystic and solid components on MRI

shortlist.label: Trigeminal schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Less common but plausible cause of cerebellopontine angle syndrome with involvement of Meckel’s cave

shortlist.label: Cystic meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of cystic and solid components on MRI with compression of adjacent structures

shortlist.label: Epidermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of cerebellopontine angle syndrome with cystic areas on MRI and gradual onset of symptoms

raw.rationale: The tumor's location centered at the left cerebellopontine angle, involvement and expansion of Meckel's cave, and extension into the left infratemporal fossa via the foramen ovale are consistent with a trigeminal schwannoma, which typically arises from the trigeminal nerve and can have a complex, lobulated appearance with cystic and solid components.

rejected.label: Vestibular schwannoma
rejected.why: Typically centered at the internal auditory canal, which is not the primary location of the mass in this case

rejected.label: Meningioma
rejected.why: While meningiomas can have a similar appearance, the specific involvement of Meckel's cave and extension into the infratemporal fossa is more suggestive of a trigeminal schwannoma

rejected.label: Cystic meningioma
rejected.why: The presence of hemorrhagic foci and the specific pattern of cystic areas with interspersed enhancing septa are not typical for meningiomas

rejected.label: Epidermoid cyst
rejected.why: Epidermoid cysts typically have a more uniform appearance on MRI, without solid components or hemorrhagic foci, and do not usually cause significant mass effect or compression of surrounding structures
